body.statement:
The frozen Gaussian quadratic local-gap law is not valid on the displayed classes.  First, for an admissible choice of the fixed constants there exist a sequence \(\mathbf P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{reg}}\) and an interior deterministic prefix \(k_n/n_{\mathcal E}\to 1/2\) for which
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,k_n}-\tau_n-b_{n,k_n}\}
\]
has a non-Gaussian subsequential limit.  Hence the asserted all-prefix \(o_{\mathbb P_n}(1)\) coupling to \(G_n\sim N(0,\Gamma_n)\) fails, and replacing \(\Gamma_n\) by another covariance matrix cannot by itself repair that coordinate.  Second, whenever the feasibility conditions of \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}support\text{-}tie\text{-}witness}\) hold, there is a sequence in \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{legal}}\) and prefixes \(k_n^{\dagger}\) and \(0\) such that, for every sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \rho_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}=\rho_{n,0},
 \qquad
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}d_n(k_n^{\dagger},0)>0,
 \qquad
 \omega^{\star}(0)>0.
\]
Thus neither the frozen Gaussian all-prefix coupling nor exact leading-MSE tie invariance is available from the stated primitive conditions.
body.justification: The corrected headline records the two proved obstructions that prevent the frozen Gaussian quadratic law from describing the generated fixed-cardinality selector.
body.gap: Neither fixed-prefix theory nor a density margin accounts for the empirical rank-boundary contribution, and exact leading-risk ties do not force target-coordinate ties.
body.consumer: A valid selected-ATE law and multiplier interval must replace the frozen process and localize over target-stable near minimizers.
body.proof_tex:
The first assertion is exactly the counterexample established by \(\mathrm{thm:generated\text{-}prefix\text{-}coupling}\).  To spell out why it rules out the asserted all-prefix approximation, let \(k_n\) be the deterministic interior prefix supplied there.  Any coupling satisfying
\[
 \max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}
 \left|
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,k}-\tau_n-b_{n,k}\}-G_{n,k}
 \right|=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1) \tag{1}
\]
would, by retaining the single term indexed by \(k_n\), imply
\[
 \left|
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,k_n}-\tau_n-b_{n,k_n}\}-G_{n,k_n}
 \right|=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1). \tag{2}
\]
But the cited core theorem proves that the statistic on the left of (2) before subtraction has a subsequential limit \(Z+H(X)\), where \(Z\) is Gaussian, \(H(X)\) is bounded, nonconstant, and independent of \(Z\), and \(Z+H(X)\) is non-Gaussian.  In contrast, every coordinate of every centered Gaussian process is Gaussian.  Equation (2) would force the two marginal laws to have bounded-Lipschitz distance tending to zero: for every real function \(f\) bounded by one and with Lipschitz constant at most one,
\[
 \left|E f(S_n)-E f(G_{n,k_n})\right|
 \le E\min\{2,|S_n-G_{n,k_n}|\}\longrightarrow0, \tag{3}
\]
where \(S_n=\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,k_n}-\tau_n-b_{n,k_n}\}\).  The convergence in (3) follows because, for each \(u>0\),
\[
 E\min\{2,|S_n-G_{n,k_n}|\}
 \le u+2\mathbb P_n\{|S_n-G_{n,k_n}|>u\},
\]
and (2) makes the probability tend to zero, after which \(u\downarrow0\).  This contradicts the proved non-Gaussian subsequential limit.  Therefore (1) fails.  More generally, suppose a covariance-only repair coupled \(S_n\) within \(o_{\mathbb P_n}(1)\) of a centered Gaussian variable with variance \(v_n\).  Along the counterexample's convergent subsequence, tightness of \(S_n\) and the coupling would make those Gaussian variables tight.  A centered normal family is tight only if \(v_n\) is bounded; after passage to a further subsequence, \(v_n\to v\ge0\), so the Gaussian variables converge to \(N(0,v)\).  The coupling would then make the same subsequence of \(S_n\) converge to \(N(0,v)\), contradicting its non-Gaussian limit.  Thus changing only a covariance matrix cannot repair the coordinate.  The counterexample's omitted term is the empirical fixed-cardinality quantile-boundary term, so the obstruction is a distributional boundary correction, not merely a covariance correction.

For the second assertion, apply \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}support\text{-}tie\text{-}witness}\) under its displayed feasibility conditions.  That theorem establishes membership of its construction in \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{legal}}\) and, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \rho_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}=\rho_{n,0},
 \qquad
 d_n(k_n^{\dagger},0)^2
 \ge B_n^2(a_n^{\dagger})^2
 \longrightarrow D_\infty>0. \tag{4}
\]
Taking square roots in (4), justified because all terms are nonnegative, gives
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}d_n(k_n^{\dagger},0)
 \ge \sqrt{D_\infty}>0. \tag{5}
\]
The same theorem applies the definition of the sharp modulus to the exact equalities in (4) and proves
\[
 \omega^{\star}(0)\ge\sqrt{D_\infty}>0. \tag{6}
\]
Equations (1)--(3) prove failure of the frozen Gaussian all-prefix coupling, while (4)--(6) prove failure of exact leading-MSE tie invariance.  These are precisely the two conclusions in the corrected statement.
